questions.prompt: What precondition must hold for Dijkstra's algorithm to be correct?

options.text: There are no more than V edges

questions.explanation: Dijkstra finalizes a vertex's distance when first extracted; a negative edge could later offer a cheaper route, which it would never revisit.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm can detect a negative-weight cycle?
questions.explanation: After V-1 relaxation rounds, if any edge can still be relaxed, Bellman-Ford has detected a reachable negative cycle.

questions.prompt: Which statements are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Dijkstra is greedy and uses a priority queue
Dijkstra correctly handles negative edge weights

questions.explanation: Dijkstra is a greedy, heap-based, non-negative-weight algorithm; Bellman-Ford is O(V·E). Dijkstra does NOT handle negative edges.

questions.prompt: The operation that updates dist[v] to dist[u] + w when a shorter path via u is found is called ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Relaxation is the shared core of both algorithms; they differ only in the order and number of relaxations.

questions.prompt: Order the main steps of Dijkstra's algorithm.

items.text: Set dist[source] = 0 and all others to infinity
Push the source into a min-priority queue
Relax its outgoing edges and repeat

questions.explanation: Initialize distances, seed the heap with the source, then repeatedly extract the nearest vertex and relax its edges.

questions.prompt: Match each item with its description.
questions.explanation: Dijkstra is fast but restricted; Bellman-Ford is general; relaxation is shared; a negative cycle removes any well-defined shortest path.
